name: When is it time to replace a bathroom countertop instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When is it time to replace a bathroom countertop instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacement if your current top has persistent water damage, deep chips, broken seams, or unsealed grout lines that harbor mold. Many homeowners also replace their top during a fixture update, since older surfaces often have fixed, three-hole four-inch faucet spreads that cannot accept modern single-hole or widespread faucets. If your existing vanity is functionally solid but visually dated, replacing just the countertop and sink creates an updated look without the expense of a full cabinet tear-out.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace your countertop if it has structural cracks, extensive moisture damage, or incompatible faucet cutouts, or when you want an update without replacing entire cabinets.
